source_review.notes: Checked every structured reference for identity, publication or update date, and cited scope. Current official GitHub merge-queue documentation supports latest-target and preceding-queue composition, merge-group CI triggers, temporary queue revisions, FIFO behavior, group controls, failure removal, descendant reconstruction, and priority-reorder rebuilds. Current official GitLab merge-train documentation supports A, A+B, A+B+C prefix pipelines, predecessor ordering, failed-member removal, redundant-pipeline cancellation, successor reconstruction, and parallel pipeline limits. Verified Humble/Farley and Duvall/Matyas/Glover bibliographic metadata for delivery and CI foundations. Current Google Engineering Practices supports self-contained small changes and their review, merge, and rollback benefits. Checked Fowler's Continuous Integration article identity and 2024 update. Checked 2026-09-06.

Checked tuple ordering, recursive equality, inequality, ellipsis, quantified policy predicate, and time-difference notation and all GitHub math delimiters.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Merge failure is explicitly typed, and deterministic merge is a model assumption rather than a universal version-control property.

evidence: Executed merge-queue-prefix-model under CPython 3.14.4 and matched seven exact outputs with empty stderr and exit status zero.
Recomputed base load 5 and limit 10, A alone as 7 <= 10, B alone as 5 <= 6, A+B and A+B+C as 7 <= 6 false, and rebuilt A+C as 7 <= 10 true.
Checked the capacity exercise: one sequential 20-minute slot provides at most three successful groups per hour, below 25 arrivals per hour, before failures or setup.
Checked old A+B+C and rebuilt A+C dictionaries differ while two independent A+C constructions have identical sorted content tuples.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All rates and configurations are explicit teaching scenarios, not observations from a repository.

Removed c_j and checked every later recursive prefix receives a changed predecessor input, yielding q_i' in the general case.
Checked that R(q,p,e) is intentionally subject-specific and cannot be substituted for R(q',p,e) without an explicit equivalence argument.
Checked admission latency and throughput definitions and their boundary qualifications.
